answer: Every identity must harbor one sealed payload whose key is bound to its own address, and a raven arrives at an unpredictable zephyr moment each epoch to demand the plaintext within ninety seconds. The payload is re-encrypted after every reveal, so an earlier copy is worthless. Running a thousand aliases therefore means truly storing a thousand distinct payloads on live disk, not one shared file: a farm pays storage and bandwidth per head, every epoch, forever, while an honest agent holds one small blob it already has.
